doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Big bands at the Greystone Ballroom and Wall Lake Casino
summary: He heard Earl Hines, Armstrong and Basie in Detroit-area ballrooms in the late 1930s-40s.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well, this is a little bit of a digression, but you were mentioning last night where you went to see big bands last night, in Detroit?
There was a place called the Greystone Ballroom. There was also a place called Wall Lake Casino. It was about 18 miles outside of Detroit at a lake, Wall Lake.

It was a big dancing casino there. A lot of the big bands played there. Most of the bands played at the Greystone Ballroom. I heard Earl Hines there. I heard Earl Hines in Flint Michigan by the way. Louis Armstrong I heard the Greystone, Count Basie, and let's see, who else? Actually, those with… Lester I didn't hear there. I never saw Lester's band in person, but they made some good records. The Greystone ballroom was the kind of place most of the big bands played.
This was in what period? What was in the late 40s or early 50s?
I would say it was in the late 30s 40s and early 50s. I think it later became something else. They tended in the something else. It lost its status.
But you era was late 30s or early 40s?
